Method of Attack: Backdoor trojan used in targeted attacks against Japanese companies to exfiltrate sensitive data
Malware inflated with junk data to avoid detection and delay investigations
Injection into processes such as Internet Explorer (iexplorer.exe), Windows Explorer (explorer.exe), and Local Security Authority Subsystem Service (lsass.exe)
Downloading and installing Mimkatz password-dumping utility to steal credentials
Lateral movement inside company networks using stolen credentials
Use of steganography to hide second-stage malware downloads inside JPG images
Use of PHP tunnel for command and control communications
Attack Vector: User downloads malware from compromised websites
Indicators of Compromise: Large malware files ranging from 50 to 200 MB containing junk data
Injection into iexplorer.exe, explorer.exe, lsass.exe processes
Use of Mimkatz module for credential dumping
C&C communications using steganography in JPG images and PHP tunnel
